title.zh: 卷一百十四 列傳第一: 后妃一
title.raw: 卷一百十四 列傳第一: 后妃一 Volume 114 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts 1

sentences.zh: 后妃一

translations.literal: Empresses and Consorts I
translations.idiomatic: Empresses and Consorts I

sentences.zh: 太祖光獻翼聖皇后，名孛兒臺旭真，弘吉剌氏，特薛禪之女也。

translations.literal: Taizu's Empress Guangxian Yisheng, named Börte, titled Lady Ujin, of the Kongirat clan, was the daughter of Dei Sechen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's empress posthumously titled Guangxian Yisheng was Börte, styled Lady Ujin, of the Kongirat clan and daughter of Dei Sechen.

sentences.zh: 特薛禪與子按陳從太祖征伐有功，賜號國舅，封王爵，以統其部族。

translations.literal: Dei Sechen and his son Anchün followed Taizu on campaigns with merit; they were granted the title Imperial Uncle, enfeoffed with princely rank, and put in charge of their tribal division.
translations.idiomatic: Dei Sechen and his son Anchün served Taizu on campaign with distinction, were granted the title Imperial Uncle and enfeoffed as kings, and were placed over their tribal division.

sentences.zh: 有旨：「生女為后，生男尚公主，世世不絕。」

translations.literal: An edict declared: "Daughters born shall become empresses; sons born shall marry princesses, generation after generation without end."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order declared: "Daughters born to this house shall be empresses; sons born shall marry imperial princesses—thus from age to age without end."

sentences.zh: 世祖至元二年十二月，追謚光獻翼聖皇后。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhiyuan, Shizu posthumously enfeoffed her as Empress Guangxian Yisheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhiyuan 2, Kublai posthumously enfeoffed her as Empress Guangxian Yisheng.

sentences.zh: 冊文曰：「尊祖宗，致誠孝，實王政之攸先；

translations.literal: The patent read: "Honoring the ancestors and practicing utmost filial piety are truly foremost in true kingship;
translations.idiomatic: The enfeoffment text read: "Honoring the ancestors and practicing utmost filial piety are truly the first duties of kingship;

sentences.zh: 法天地，建鴻名，亦母儀之克稱。

translations.literal: Taking heaven and earth as model and establishing a great name is also what fully befits a mother's standard.
translations.idiomatic: taking heaven and earth as one's model and establishing a great name is likewise what fully befits the standard of a mother of the realm.

sentences.zh: 肆先虔於太室，庸昭示於后昆，體茲至公，節以大惠。

translations.literal: We therefore first offer sincerity in the Grand Temple, broadly proclaim it to posterity, embody this supreme impartiality, and regulate it with great grace.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore first offer sincerity in the Grand Temple, broadly proclaim this to posterity, embody supreme impartiality, and temper it with great grace.

sentences.zh: 欽惟光獻皇后，宅收淵靜，稟德柔嘉，當聖神創業之初，有夙夜求賢之助。

translations.literal: Reverently considering Empress Guangxian — dwelling in deep stillness, endowed with gentle excellence — at the beginning when the sage founded the enterprise she had the assistance of working through the nights to seek the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently considering Empress Guangxian, who dwelt in deep stillness and was endowed with gentle excellence: at the beginning of the sage founder's enterprise she lent the aid of laboring through the nights to seek out the worthy.

sentences.zh: 功施社稷，垂慈訓於景襄；

translations.literal: Her merit extended to the altars of state; she bestowed kindly instruction upon Jingxiang;
translations.idiomatic: Her merit reached the altars of state; she bestowed kindly instruction upon Jingxiang;

sentences.zh: 慶衍宮闈，流徽音於莊聖。

translations.literal: Her blessing spread through the palace; she passed down fine fame to Zhuang Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: her blessing spread through the inner palace and passed down fine renown to Zhuang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 協贊龍飛之運，永詒燕翼之謀。

translations.literal: She assisted the fortune of the dragon's flight and forever bequeathed the plan of sheltering the fledglings.
translations.idiomatic: She assisted the fortune of the dragon's ascent and forever bequeathed the plan of sheltering the fledglings.

sentences.zh: 惟周人著稱《思齊》，亦推本興王之跡；

translations.literal: The Zhou people gave renown to the 《Si Qi》 and also traced back to the traces of the founding king;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou gave renown to the 《Si Qi》 and likewise traced their rise back to the founding king;

sentences.zh: 在漢世始謚光烈，蓋篤申追遠之情。

translations.literal: In the Han dynasty they first posthumously titled Guanglie, truly deepening the feeling of honoring the remote past.
translations.idiomatic: in Han they first posthumously titled Guanglie, truly deepening the feeling of honoring those long gone.

sentences.zh: 是用稽迪舊章，增崇遺美。

translations.literal: Therefore we examine and follow the old statutes and augment and exalt her departed excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we examine and follow the old statutes and augment the praise of her departed excellence.

sentences.zh: 謹遣攝太尉某，奉玉冊玉寶，加上尊謚曰光獻翼聖皇后。

translations.literal: We respectfully send the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies to present jade registers and jade seals and add the honorific posthumous title Empress Guangxian Yisheng.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully send the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies to present jade registers and jade seals and add the honorific posthumous title Empress Guangxian Yisheng.

sentences.zh: 伏惟淑靈降格，典禮備膺，於億萬年，茂隆丕祚。」

translations.literal: Humbly considering that her pure spirit descends and the rites are fully received — through ten thousand years may your great fortune flourish abundantly."
translations.idiomatic: Humbly: may her pure spirit descend, the rites be fully received, and through ten thousand years your great fortune flourish abundantly."

sentences.zh: 升祔太祖廟。

translations.literal: Her tablet was elevated to join Taizu in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Her tablet was elevated to join Taizu in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 其餘后妃，有四斡耳朵四十餘人，不記氏族，其名悉見於《表》。

translations.literal: Of the other empresses and consorts, in the four ordas there were more than forty persons whose clans are not recorded; their names all appear in the 《Tables》.
translations.idiomatic: As for the other empresses and consorts, in the four ordas there were more than forty women whose clans are not recorded; their names all appear in the 《Tables》.

sentences.zh: 后皆仿此。

translations.literal: Empresses below all follow this model.
translations.idiomatic: The accounts of empresses below all follow this pattern.

sentences.zh: 太宗昭慈皇后，名脫列哥那，乃馬真氏，生定宗。

translations.literal: Taizong's Empress Zhaoci was named Töregene, of the Naiman clan; she bore Dingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's Empress Zhaoci was named Töregene, of the Naiman clan, and bore Dingzong.

sentences.zh: 歲辛丑十一月，太宗崩，后稱制攝國者五年。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the xinchou year Taizong died; the empress held the regency and governed the realm for five years.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the xinchou year Taizong died; the empress held the regency and governed the realm for five years.

sentences.zh: 丙午，會諸王百官，議立定宗。

translations.literal: In the bingwu year she convened the princes and the hundred officials to deliberate on establishing Dingzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingwu year she convened the princes and officials to deliberate on establishing Dingzong as emperor.

sentences.zh: 朝政多出於后。

translations.literal: Court government largely issued from the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Most affairs of state issued from the empress.

sentences.zh: 至元二年崩，追謚詔慈皇后，升祔太宗廟。

translations.literal: She died in the second year of Zhiyuan and was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhaoci; her tablet was elevated to join Taizong in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Zhiyuan 2 and was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhaoci; her tablet was elevated to join Taizong in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 定宗欽淑皇后，名斡兀立海迷失。

translations.literal: Dingzong's Empress Qinshu was named Ögul Qaimish.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzong's Empress Qinshu was named Ögul Qaimish.

sentences.zh: 定宗崩，后抱子失列門垂簾聽政者六月。

translations.literal: When Dingzong died, the empress held her son Shiremun and ruled from behind the curtain for six months.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingzong died, the empress held her son Shiremun on her lap and ruled from behind the curtain for six months.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，追謚欽淑皇后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Qinshu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Qinshu.

sentences.zh: 憲宗貞節皇后，名忽都臺，弘吉剌氏，特薛禪孫忙哥陳之女也，蚤崩，后妹也速兒繼為妃。

translations.literal: Xianzong's Empress Zhenjie was named Qututai, of the Kongirat clan, daughter of Manggechen, grandson of Dei Sechen; she died young, and her younger sister Yesuer succeeded as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong's Empress Zhenjie was named Qututai, of the Kongirat clan and daughter of Manggechen, grandson of Dei Sechen; she died young, and her younger sister Yesuer succeeded as consort.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，追謚貞節皇后，升祔憲宗廟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhenjie; her tablet was elevated to join Xianzong in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhenjie and her tablet was elevated to join Xianzong in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 世祖昭睿順聖皇后，名察必，弘吉剌氏，濟寧忠武王按陳之女也。

translations.literal: Shizu's Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng was named Chabi, of the Kongirat clan, daughter of Anchün, loyal and martial King of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu's Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng was Chabi, of the Kongirat clan and daughter of Anchün, loyal and martial King of Jining.

sentences.zh: 生裕宗。

translations.literal: She bore Yuzong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Yuzong.

sentences.zh: 中統初，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongtong she was established as empress.

sentences.zh: 至元十年三月，授冊寶，上尊號貞懿昭聖順天睿文光應皇后。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year of Zhiyuan she was invested with registers and seals and given the honorific title Empress Zhenyi Zhaosheng Shuntian Ruìwen Guangying.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhiyuan 10 she received registers and seals and was given the honorific title Empress Zhenyi Zhaosheng Shuntian Ruìwen Guangying.

sentences.zh: 一日，四怯薛官奏割京城外近地牧馬，帝既允，方以圖進。

translations.literal: One day an official of the four keshig memorialized to allot nearby land outside the capital for pasturing horses; the emperor had already assented and the map was just being presented.
translations.idiomatic: One day an official of the four keshig memorialized to allot nearby land outside the capital for pasturing horses; the emperor had already assented and the map was about to be submitted.

sentences.zh: 后至帝前，將諫，先陽責太保劉秉忠曰：「汝漢人聰明者，言則帝聽，汝何為不諫？

translations.literal: The empress came before the emperor intending to remonstrate; she first openly rebuked Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong, saying: "You are a clever Han man — when you speak the emperor listens; why did you not remonstrate?
translations.idiomatic: The empress came before the emperor intending to remonstrate; she first openly rebuked Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong: "You are a clever Han man, and when you speak the emperor listens — why did you not remonstrate?

sentences.zh: 向初到定都時，若以地牧馬則可，今軍蘸俱分業已定，奪之可乎？」

translations.literal: When we first chose the site for the capital, grazing there would have been acceptable; now the military households and postal stations have all been assigned their occupations — can we take the land away?"
translations.idiomatic: When we first chose the site for the capital, grazing there would have been fine; but now the military households and postal stations have all been assigned their occupations — can we take the land away?"

sentences.zh: 帝默然，命寢其事。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent and ordered the matter shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent and ordered the matter shelved.

sentences.zh: 后嘗於太府監支繒帛表裏各一，帝謂后曰：「此軍國所需，非私家物，后何可得支？」

translations.literal: The empress once drew from the Directorate of Palace Supplies one bolt each of outer and lining silk; the emperor said to her: "These are needed for army and state, not private goods — how can the empress draw them?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress once drew from the Directorate of Palace Supplies one bolt each of outer and lining silk; the emperor told her, "These are needed for army and state, not private goods — how can the empress draw on them?"

sentences.zh: 后自是率宮人親執女工，拘諸舊弓弦練之，緝為綢，以為衣，其韌密比綾綺。

translations.literal: From then on the empress led the palace women in doing needlework herself, collected old bowstrings and boiled them, wove them into silk, and made clothing; its toughness and density rivaled damask.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the empress led the palace women in needlework herself, collected old bowstrings and boiled them down, wove them into cloth, and made garments whose toughness and density rivaled damask.

sentences.zh: 宣徽院羊臑皮置不用，后取之，合縫為地毯。

translations.literal: Sheep-flank hides set aside unused by the Xuanhui Court she took and stitched together into carpets.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep-flank hides set aside unused by the Xuanhui Court she took and stitched together into carpets.

sentences.zh: 其勤儉有節而無棄物，類如此。

translations.literal: Her diligence, thrift, and restraint without discarding usable things were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Her diligence, thrift, and refusal to waste usable materials were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 十三年，平宋，幼主朝於上都。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Song was pacified and the young ruler came to court at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Song was pacified and the young Song ruler came to court at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 大宴，眾皆歡甚，唯后不樂。

translations.literal: At a great banquet all were exceedingly joyful; only the empress was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At a great banquet everyone was exceedingly joyful; only the empress was not pleased.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我今平江南，自此不用兵甲，眾人皆喜，爾獨不樂，何耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have now pacified Jiangnan; from this time forth we need no more arms and armor; everyone is pleased — you alone are not pleased; why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have now pacified the south; from this time forth we need no more arms and armor; everyone is pleased — you alone are not. Why?"

sentences.zh: 后跪奏曰：「妾聞自古無千歲之國，毋使吾子孫及此，則幸矣。」

translations.literal: The empress knelt and memorialized: "Your servant has heard that from antiquity there has been no state of a thousand years; if only our sons and grandsons do not come to this, it will be fortunate enough."
translations.idiomatic: The empress knelt and said, "Your servant has heard that from antiquity no state has lasted a thousand years; if only our sons and grandsons do not come to this, it will be fortune enough."

sentences.zh: 帝以宋府庫故物各聚置殿庭上，召后視之，后遍視即去。

translations.literal: The emperor had the old goods from the Song treasury all gathered and set out in the palace courtyard and summoned the empress to view them; she looked them all over and left at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the old goods from the Song treasury gathered in the palace courtyard and summoned the empress to view them; she looked them all over and left at once.

sentences.zh: 帝遣宦者追問后，欲何所取。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a eunuch after the empress to ask what she wished to take.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a eunuch after the empress to ask what she wished to take.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「宋人貯蓄以遺其子孫，子孫不能守，而歸於我，我何忍取一物耶！」

translations.literal: The empress said: "The Song people stored these up to bequeath to their sons and grandsons; their sons and grandsons could not keep them, and they have come to us — how could I bear to take a single thing!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "The Song stored these up for their sons and grandsons; their sons and grandsons could not keep them, and they have come to us — how could I bear to take a single thing!"

sentences.zh: 時宋太后全氏至京，不習北方風土，后為奏令回江南。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Quan of Song had come to the capital and was unaccustomed to the northern climate; the empress memorialized to have her sent back to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dowager Quan of Song had come to the capital and was unaccustomed to the northern climate; the empress memorialized to have her sent back to the south.

sentences.zh: 帝不允，至三奏，帝乃答曰：「爾婦人無遠慮，若使之南還，或浮言一動，即廢其家，非所以愛之也。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent; after three memorials he answered: "You women lack far-sightedness; if we sent her south, a single floating rumor might at once bring ruin on her house — that is not how to love her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not consent; after three memorials he answered, "You women lack far-sightedness; if we sent her south, a single rumor might at once bring ruin on her house — that is not how to show love.

sentences.zh: 茍能愛之，時加存恤，使之便安可也。」

translations.literal: If we can love her, from time to time show care and relief and make her comfortable, that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: If we truly love her, we need only show care and relief from time to time and make her comfortable — that will suffice."

sentences.zh: 后退，益厚待之。

translations.literal: The empress withdrew and treated her all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: The empress withdrew and treated her all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 胡帽舊無前檐，帝因射日色炫目，以語后，后即益前檐。

translations.literal: Mongol caps formerly had no front brim; the emperor, while shooting, found the sunlight dazzling and told the empress; she at once added a front brim.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol caps formerly had no front brim; while shooting the emperor found the sunlight dazzling and told the empress, who at once added a front brim.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，遂命為式。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it made the standard pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it made the standard pattern.

sentences.zh: 又制一衣，前有裳無衽，后長倍於前，亦無領袖，綴以兩襻，名曰比甲，以便弓馬，時皆仿之。

translations.literal: She also devised a garment with a skirt in front but no overlapping lapel, the back twice as long as the front, likewise without collar or sleeves, fastened with two loops — called a bijia — to facilitate archery and horsemanship; all at the time copied it.
translations.idiomatic: She also devised a garment with a skirt panel in front but no overlapping lapel, the back twice as long as the front and likewise without collar or sleeves, fastened with two loops and called a bijia, to facilitate archery and horsemanship; everyone at the time copied it.

sentences.zh: 后性明敏，達於事機，國家初政，左右匡正，當時與有力焉。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature intelligent and clear, adept at affairs; in the founding government of the state she corrected matters left and right, and at the time she had real force.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was intelligent and clear by nature and adept at affairs; in the founding government of the state she corrected matters on every side, and at the time she wielded real influence.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月崩。

translations.literal: She died in the second month of the eighteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the second month of the eighteenth year.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗即位，五月，追謚昭睿順聖皇后，其冊文曰：「奉先思孝，臣子之至情；

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Chengzong took the throne; in the fifth month she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng; the patent read: "Serving the former and thinking of filial piety are the utmost feeling of subject and child;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year Chengzong took the throne; in the fifth month she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng. The enfeoffment text read: "Serving the former and thinking of filial piety are the utmost feeling of subject and child;

sentences.zh: 節惠易名，古今之大典。

translations.literal: Restraining grace and changing names are the great statutes of antiquity and today.
translations.idiomatic: restraining grace during mourning and changing names are the great statutes of antiquity and today.

sentences.zh: 惟殷娥有明德之號，而周任著《思齊》之稱。

translations.literal: Yin E had the title of Bright Virtue, and Zhou Ren gave renown to the 《Si Qi》.
translations.idiomatic: Yin E bore the title of Bright Virtue, and Zhou Ren gave renown to the 《Si Qi》.

sentences.zh: 爰考舊章，式崇尊諡。

translations.literal: We therefore examine the old statutes and exalt the honorific posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore examine the old statutes and exalt the honorific posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 恭惟先皇后，厚德載物，正位承天。

translations.literal: Reverently considering the late empress: her thick virtue bore all things; she took the correct position and received heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently considering the late empress: her thick virtue bore all things; she took the correct position and received heaven.

sentences.zh: 隆內治於公宮，綱大倫於天下。

translations.literal: She elevated inner governance in the public palace and set the great bonds in order throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: She elevated inner governance in the palace and set the great bonds in order throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 曩事龍潛之邸，及乘虎變之秋。

translations.literal: Long ago she served in the lodge of the hidden dragon; when the tiger's transformation came in autumn she was there.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago she served in the lodge of the hidden dragon; when the season of the tiger's transformation came she was there.

sentences.zh: 鄂渚班師，洞識事機之會；

translations.literal: When the army withdrew at Ezhou she deeply understood the moment of opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew at Ezhou she deeply understood the moment of opportunity;

sentences.zh: 上都踐祚，居多輔佐之謀。

translations.literal: when the throne was taken at Shangdu she largely supplied plans of assistance.
translations.idiomatic: when the throne was taken at Shangdu she largely supplied plans of assistance.

sentences.zh: 先物之明，獨斷於衷；

translations.literal: Foreknowledge of things — she alone decided in her heart;
translations.idiomatic: Foreknowledge of things — she alone decided in her heart;

sentences.zh: 進賢之志，允葉於上。

translations.literal: her will to advance the worthy truly accorded with her lord above.
translations.idiomatic: her will to advance the worthy truly accorded with her lord above.

sentences.zh: 左右我聖祖，建帝王之極功；

translations.literal: She assisted our sage ancestor and established the utmost merit of emperors and kings;
translations.idiomatic: She assisted our sage ancestor and established the utmost merit of emperors and kings;

sentences.zh: 撫育我前人，嗣社稷之重托。

translations.literal: she nurtured our forebear and succeeded to the heavy charge of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: she nurtured our forebear and succeeded to the heavy charge of the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 臣下之勸勞灼見，生民之疾苦周知。

translations.literal: The toil and merit of officials were clearly seen; the suffering of the people was fully known.
translations.idiomatic: The toil and merit of officials were clearly seen; the suffering of the people was fully known.

sentences.zh: 儷宸極二十年，垂慈範千萬世。

translations.literal: She matched the apex of heaven for twenty years and bestowed a model of kindness for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: She matched the apex of heaven for twenty years and bestowed a model of kindness for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 惟全美聖而益聖，宜顯冊書而屢書。

translations.literal: Only when fully beautiful in sagehood and ever more sage should registers be displayed and written again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Only when fully beautiful in sagehood and ever more sage should registers be displayed and written again and again.

translations.literal: Mingzong's Empress Zhenyu Huisheng was named Mailaiti; she bore Shundi and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong's Empress Zhenyu Huisheng was named Mailaiti. She bore Shundi and then died.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，謚貞裕徽聖皇后。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne, the posthumous title Empress Zhenyu Huisheng was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, she was given the posthumous title Empress Zhenyu Huisheng.

sentences.zh: 八不沙皇后，成宗甥壽寧公主之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Babusha was the daughter of Princess Shouning, Chengzong's niece by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Babusha was the daughter of Princess Shouning, a niece by marriage of Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 侍明宗潛邸，生寧宗。

translations.literal: She attended Mingzong in his hidden residence and bore Ningzong.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Mingzong while he was still heir and bore Ningzong.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，立寧徽寺，掌明宗皇后宮事，以鈔萬錠、幣帛二千匹，供後宮費用。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli the Ninghui Temple was established to manage the affairs of Mingzong's empresses' palaces, with ten thousand ingots of paper money and two thousand bolts of silks and cloth supplied for the rear palaces' expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 2 the Ninghui Temple was established to manage Mingzong's empresses' palace affairs, with ten thousand ingots of paper money and two thousand bolts of silk and cloth supplied for the rear palaces.

sentences.zh: 十一月，后請為明宗資冥福，命帝師率諸僧作佛事七日於大天源延聖寺，道士建醮於玉虛、天寶、太乙、萬壽四宮，及武當、龍虎二山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the empress requested merit for Mingzong's salvation in the afterlife; the emperor ordered the Imperial Preceptor to lead the monks in Buddhist rites for seven days at the Great Tianyuan Yansheng Temple, and Daoist masters to perform offerings at the four palaces of Yuxu, Tianbao, Taiyi, and Wanshou, and on Mount Wudang and Mount Longhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the empress requested merit for Mingzong's salvation in the afterlife. The emperor ordered the Imperial Preceptor to lead monks in seven days of Buddhist rites at the Great Tianyuan Yansheng Temple, and Daoist masters to perform offerings at the Yuxu, Tianbao, Taiyi, and Wanshou palaces and on Mount Wudang and Mount Longhu.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，敕有司供明宗後宮幣帛二百匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun an edict ordered the relevant offices to supply two hundred bolts of silks and cloth to Mingzong's rear palaces.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1 an edict ordered the relevant offices to supply two hundred bolts of silk and cloth to Mingzong's rear palaces.

sentences.zh: 是年四月崩。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fourth month of that year.

sentences.zh: 文宗卜答失裏皇后，弘吉剌氏，父駙馬魯王雕阿不剌，母魯國公主桑哥剌吉。

translations.literal: Wenzong's Empress Budashiri was of the Kongirat clan; her father was the imperial son-in-law Prince Lu Diaobula; her mother was Princess Lu Sangoraji.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong's Empress Budashiri was of the Kongirat clan. Her father was the imperial son-in-law Prince Lu Diaobula, and her mother was Princess Lu Sangoraji.

sentences.zh: 文宗居建業，后亦在行。

translations.literal: When Wenzong resided at Jianye, the empress was also on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong was at Jianye, the empress accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 天歷元年，文宗即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli Wenzong took the throne and she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 1 Wenzong took the throne and she was established as empress.

sentences.zh: 二年，授冊寶。

translations.literal: In the second year registers and seals were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year registers and seals were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，后以銀五萬兩助建大承天護聖寺。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the empress contributed fifty thousand taels of silver toward building the Great Chengtian Husheng Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month she gave fifty thousand taels of silver toward building the Great Chengtian Husheng Temple.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，以籍沒張珪家田四百頃，賜護聖寺為永業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun four hundred qing of fields confiscated from Zhang Gui's household were granted to the Husheng Temple as perpetual property.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1 four hundred qing of fields confiscated from Zhang Gui's household were granted to the Husheng Temple as perpetual property.

sentences.zh: 后與宦者拜住謀殺明宗后八不沙。

translations.literal: The empress plotted with the eunuch Baiju to murder Mingzong's empress Babusha.
translations.idiomatic: The empress conspired with the eunuch Baiju to have Mingzong's empress Babusha killed.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，文宗崩於上都，后導揚末命，申帝初誌，遂立明宗次子懿璘質班，是為寧宗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year Wenzong died at Shangdu; the empress guided his final command and declared the emperor's original intent, whereupon she established Mingzong's second son Yishiliban—this was Ningzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year Wenzong died at Shangdu. The empress guided his final command and declared the emperor's original intent, establishing Mingzong's second son Yishiliban as emperor—this was Ningzong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，奉玉冊玉寶尊皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month jade registers and jade seals were presented to honor the empress as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month jade registers and jade seals were presented to honor her as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禦興聖殿受朝賀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month she received homage at the Hall of Sagacious Birth.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month she received homage at the Hall of Sagacious Birth.

sentences.zh: 寧宗崩，大臣請立太子燕貼古思。

translations.literal: When Ningzong died, the great ministers requested that the crown prince Yantiegusi be established.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong died, the chief ministers asked that Crown Prince Yantiegusi be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「天位至重，吾子尚幼，明宗長子妥歡帖睦爾在廣西，今十三歲矣，理當立之。」

translations.literal: The empress said: "The heavenly throne is of the utmost weight; my son is still young. Mingzong's eldest son Toghon Temür is in Guangxi; he is now thirteen years old. By right he should be established."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "The throne is of the utmost weight; my son is still young. Mingzong's eldest son Toghon Temür is in Guangxi and is now thirteen. By right he should be enthroned."

sentences.zh: 於是奉旨迎至京師，以明年六月即位，是為順帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon, by imperial order, he was welcomed to the capital; in the sixth month of the following year he took the throne—this was Shundi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, by imperial order, he was welcomed to the capital. In the sixth month of the following year he took the throne—this was Shundi.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，尊為太皇太后，仍稱制臨朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager and still held the regency in court.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 1 she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager and still held the regency at court.

sentences.zh: 至元六年六月，詔去尊號，安置東安州，尋崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Zhiyuan an edict removed her honorific title; she was settled at Dong'an Prefecture and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhiyuan 6 an edict stripped her honorific title. She was settled at Dong'an Prefecture and soon died.

sentences.zh: 寧宗答裏也忒迷失皇后，弘吉剌氏。

translations.literal: Ningzong's Empress Darayetemishi was of the Kongirat clan.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong's Empress Darayetemishi was of the Kongirat clan.

sentences.zh: 至順三年十月，立為后。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Zhishun she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhishun 3 she was established as empress.

sentences.zh: 至正二十八年崩，升祔寧宗廟。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhizheng she died; her tablet was elevated to join Ningzong in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 28 she died, and her tablet was placed beside Ningzong in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 順帝答納失裏皇后，欽察氏，太師平王燕鐵木兒之女。

translations.literal: Shundi's Empress Danashiri was of the Qipchaq clan, daughter of the Grand Preceptor and Prince of Ping, El Temür.
translations.idiomatic: Shundi's Empress Danashiri was of the Qipchaq clan and daughter of the Grand Preceptor and Prince of Ping, El Temür.

sentences.zh: 至順四年，立為后。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhishun she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 4 she was established as empress.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，授冊寶，其冊文曰：「天之元統二氣，配莫厚於坤儀；

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong registers and seals were bestowed; the text of the register read: "Heaven's primal Yuantong of the two qi—none is thicker in pairing than the Kun regalia;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 2 registers and seals were bestowed. The register text read: "Heaven's primal union of the two qi—none pairs more richly than the Kun regalia;

sentences.zh: 月之道循右行，明周貞於乾曜。

translations.literal: the moon's way follows the rightward course; brightness completes its constancy at the Qian radiance.
translations.idiomatic: the moon's way follows the rightward course; its brightness completes its constancy at the Qian radiance.

sentences.zh: 若昔帝王之宅後，居多輔相之世勛。

translations.literal: Of old when emperors took their consorts, many were from families of chief ministers who had served generations.
translations.idiomatic: Of old when emperors chose consorts, many came from families of chief ministers who had served for generations.

sentences.zh: 蓋選德於亢宗，亦疇庸於先正。

translations.literal: They selected virtue from the lofty clan and also enfeoffed merit in the former upright.
translations.idiomatic: They selected virtue from the eminent clan and also rewarded the merit of former ministers.

sentences.zh: 造周資任、姒之化，興漢表馬、鄧之功。

translations.literal: Zhou was aided by the transformation of Ren and Si; Han displayed the achievement of Ma and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was aided by the transformation of Ren and Si; Han displayed the achievement of Ma and Deng.

sentences.zh: 咨爾皇后欽察氏，雍肅惠慈，謙裕靜淑。

translations.literal: We address you, Empress of the Qipchaq clan: dignified, solemn, gracious, and compassionate; humble, ample, quiet, and pure.
translations.idiomatic: We address you, Empress of the Qipchaq clan—dignified, solemn, gracious, and compassionate; humble, ample, quiet, and pure.

sentences.zh: 乃祖乃父，夙堅翼亮之心；

translations.literal: Your grandfathers and fathers from of old held firm the heart of winged assistance;
translations.idiomatic: Your grandfathers and fathers long held firm the heart of loyal assistance;

sentences.zh: 於國於家，實獲修齊之助。

translations.literal: for state and family they truly gained the help of cultivation and ordering.
translations.idiomatic: for state and family they truly won the help of self-cultivation and good governance.

sentences.zh: 朕纘丕圖之初載，親承太后之睿謨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of my continuing the great plan I personally received the Empress Dowager's wise counsel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of my continuing the great design I personally received the Empress Dowager's wise counsel.

sentences.zh: 眷我元臣，簡茲碩媛。

translations.literal: Favoring my Yuan minister, I have chosen this great lady.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring my Yuan minister, I have chosen this great lady.

sentences.zh: 相嚴禘而率典，奉慈極以愉顏。

translations.literal: Together we solemnly perform the suburban rites and lead the statutes; we serve the compassionate apex with a pleased countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Together we solemnly perform the suburban rites and lead the statutes, serving the empress dowager with a pleased countenance.

sentences.zh: 用彰祎翟之華，式著旗常之舊。

translations.literal: Thus we display the splendor of the ceremonial robes; thus we show forth the old glory of banner and tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we display the splendor of the ceremonial robes and show forth the old glory of banner and tablet.

sentences.zh: 令攝太尉某官授以玉冊寶章，命爾為皇后。

translations.literal: Let the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies, an official, be ordered to confer the jade registers, seal, and insignia and command you to be empress.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies, an official, confer the jade registers, seal, and insignia and command you to be empress.

sentences.zh: 備成嘉禮，宏賁大猷。

translations.literal: Complete the auspicious ceremony; grandly adorn the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Complete the auspicious ceremony and grandly adorn the great design.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 嵩高生賢，予篤懷於良佐；

translations.literal: Songgao bore the worthy; I deeply cherish a good helper;
translations.idiomatic: As Songgao bore the worthy, I deeply cherish a good helper;

sentences.zh: 《關雎》正始，爾勉嗣於徽音。

translations.literal: the 《Guanju》 sets the beginning; you must strive to continue the fine repute.
translations.idiomatic: as the 《Guanju》 sets the beginning, strive to continue the fine repute.

sentences.zh: 永錫壽康，昭示悠久。」

translations.literal: Forever bestow long life and health; manifest and display endurance."
translations.idiomatic: Forever bestow long life and health; manifest endurance through the ages."

sentences.zh: 三年，后兄御史大夫唐其勢以謀逆誅，弟塔剌海走匿后宮，后以衣蔽之，因遷后出宮，丞相伯顏鴆后於開平民舍。

translations.literal: In the third year the empress's elder brother, Censor-in-Chief Tangqishi, was executed for plotting rebellion; her younger brother Talahai fled and hid in the empress's palace. The empress screened him with her robes; therefore the empress was removed from the palace, and Chancellor Bayan poisoned her at a lodge in Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the empress's elder brother, Censor-in-Chief Tangqishi, was executed for treason. Her younger brother Talahai fled into the empress's palace, and she hid him beneath her robes. She was therefore removed from the palace, and Chancellor Bayan poisoned her at a lodge in Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 伯顏忽都皇后，弘吉剌氏，宣慈惠聖皇后真哥侄毓德王孛羅帖木兒之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Bayan Qudu was of the Kongirat clan, daughter of Prince Yude Boluotiemuer, nephew of Empress Xuanci Huisheng Zhenge.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Bayan Qudu was of the Kongirat clan and daughter of Prince Yude Boluotiemuer, nephew of Empress Xuanci Huisheng Zhenge.

sentences.zh: 至元三年三月，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Zhiyuan she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhiyuan 3 she was established as empress.

sentences.zh: 其冊文曰：「帝王之道，齊其家而天下平；

translations.literal: The patent read: "The way of emperors and kings is to order the family and thereby bring peace to the realm;
translations.idiomatic: The enfeoffment text read: "The way of emperors and kings is to order the family and thereby bring peace to the realm;

sentences.zh: 風教所基，正乎位而人倫厚。

translations.literal: custom and instruction have their foundation; when the position is correct, human bonds grow thick.
translations.idiomatic: custom and instruction have their foundation; when the position is correct, human bonds grow strong.

sentences.zh: 爰擇配以承宗事，若稽古以率典常。

translations.literal: We therefore choose a consort to undertake the ancestral charge and examine antiquity to follow constant statutes.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore choose a consort to undertake the ancestral charge and examine antiquity to follow the constant statutes.

sentences.zh: 咨爾弘吉剌氏，淑哲溫恭，齊莊貞一。

translations.literal: We address you of the Kongirat clan: pure, wise, warm, and respectful; even, dignified, chaste, and unified.
translations.idiomatic: We address you of the Kongirat clan: pure, wise, warm, and respectful; even, dignified, chaste, and unified.

sentences.zh: 屬選賢於中壸，躬受命於慈闈。

translations.literal: When worthies were chosen for the inner palace, you personally received the mandate from the compassionate quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When worthies were chosen for the inner palace, you personally received the mandate from the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 勖帥來嬪，蹈榘儀之有度；

translations.literal: Urged and led, you came as consort and trod the compass of ritual with measure;
translations.idiomatic: Urged and led, you came as consort and trod the compass of ritual with measure;

sentences.zh: 動容中禮，謹夙夜以無違。

translations.literal: your bearing accorded with rites; you were careful from morning to night without violation.
translations.idiomatic: your bearing accorded with rites; you were careful from morning to night without violation.

sentences.zh: 茲表式於宮庭，宜推崇其位號。

translations.literal: Now you display the model in the palace court; it is fitting to exalt your position and title.
translations.idiomatic: Now you display the model in the palace court; it is fitting to exalt your position and title.

sentences.zh: 乃蠲吉旦，庸舉彜章，遣攝太尉某持節授以玉冊寶章，命爾為皇后。

translations.literal: We therefore choose an auspicious day and duly perform the constant statutes, sending the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies with credentials to confer jade registers, seals, and insignia and command you to be empress.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore choose an auspicious day and duly perform the constant statutes, sending the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies with credentials to confer jade registers, seals, and insignia and command you to be empress.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 乾施坤承，克順成於四序；

translations.literal: Qian bestows and Kun receives, achieving compliance and completion in the four seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven bestows and earth receives, achieving compliance and completion in the four seasons;

sentences.zh: 日明月儷，久照臨於萬方。

translations.literal: sun and moon pair in brightness, long illuminating the ten thousand regions.
translations.idiomatic: the sun and moon pair in brightness, long illuminating the ten thousand regions.

sentences.zh: 朕欲躋世於乂安，爾其助予之德化，共禦亨嘉之運，益延昌熾之期。

translations.literal: We wish to raise the age to governance and peace; you must assist Our moral transformation, together withstand the fortunate and excellent fortune, and further extend the season of flourishing brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: We wish to raise the age to governance and peace; you must assist our moral transformation, together withstand the fortunate season, and further extend the age of flourishing brilliance.

sentences.zh: 勉爾徽音，聿修內治。」

translations.literal: Strive in your fine repute and diligently cultivate inner governance."
translations.idiomatic: Strive in your fine repute and diligently cultivate inner governance."

sentences.zh: 生皇子真金，二歲而夭。

translations.literal: She bore the prince Zhenjin, who died at the age of two.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Prince Zhenjin, who died at the age of two.

sentences.zh: 后性節儉，不妒忌，動以禮法自持。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature frugal and not jealous; in her movements she upheld herself with ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was frugal by nature and not jealous; in all her conduct she upheld herself with ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 第二皇后奇氏素有寵，居興聖西宮，帝希幸東內。

translations.literal: The second empress, Lady Ki, had long enjoyed favor; she dwelt in the western palace of Xingsheng, while the emperor rarely visited the eastern inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The second empress, Lady Ki, had long enjoyed favor; she dwelt in the western palace of Xingsheng, while the emperor rarely visited the eastern inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 后左右以為言，后無幾微怨望意。

translations.literal: Those around the empress spoke of this to her, but the empress showed not the slightest resentment or longing.
translations.idiomatic: Those around the empress spoke of this to her, but she showed not the slightest resentment or longing.

sentences.zh: 從帝時巡上京，次中道，帝遣內官傳旨，欲臨幸，后辭曰：「暮夜非至尊往來之時。」

translations.literal: Following the emperor on a tour to Shangdu, they halted midway; the emperor sent a palace eunuch with an order wishing to visit her quarters. The empress declined, saying: "Evening and night are not the time for the supreme lord to come and go."
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor on a tour to Shangdu, they halted midway; the emperor sent a palace eunuch wishing to visit her quarters. The empress declined: "Evening and night are not the time for the supreme lord to come and go."

sentences.zh: 內官往復者三，竟拒不納，帝益賢之。

translations.literal: The palace eunuch went back and forth three times; she finally refused admission, and the emperor esteemed her all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch went back and forth three times; she finally refused admission, and the emperor esteemed her all the more.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問后：「中政院所支錢糧，皆傳汝旨，汝還記之否？」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked the empress: "The funds and grain disbursed by the Central Palace Administration all pass on your order — do you still remember them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked the empress, "The funds and grain disbursed by the Central Palace Administration all pass on your order — do you still remember them?"

sentences.zh: 后對曰：「妾當用則支。

translations.literal: The empress replied: "Your servant disburses when there is need.
translations.idiomatic: The empress replied, "Your servant disburses when there is need.

sentences.zh: 關防出入，必己選人司之，妾豈能盡記耶？」

translations.literal: Seals for passage in and out must be managed by persons I myself select — how could your servant remember them all?"
translations.idiomatic: Seals for passage in and out must be managed by persons I myself select — how could your servant remember them all?"

sentences.zh: 居坤德殿，終日端坐，未嘗妄逾戶閾。

translations.literal: She dwelt in the Kunde Hall, sitting upright all day, never rashly crossing the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: She dwelt in the Kunde Hall, sitting upright all day and never rashly crossing the threshold.

sentences.zh: 至正二十五年八月崩，年四十二。

translations.literal: She died in the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year of Zhiping, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eighth month of Zhiping 25, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 奇氏後見其所遺衣服弊壞，大笑曰：「正宮皇后，何至服此等衣耶！」

translations.literal: Later Lady Ki saw the worn and tattered clothes she had left behind and laughed loudly, saying: "The principal-palace empress — how could she wear clothes like these!"
translations.idiomatic: Later Lady Ki saw the worn and tattered clothes she had left behind and laughed loudly: "The principal-palace empress — how could she wear clothes like these!"

sentences.zh: 其樸素可知。

translations.literal: Her plain simplicity can thus be known.
translations.idiomatic: Her plain simplicity can thus be known.

sentences.zh: 逾月，皇太子自冀寧歸，哭之甚哀。

translations.literal: After more than a month the crown prince returned from Jining and wept for her with great grief.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the crown prince returned from Jining and wept for her with great grief.

sentences.zh: 完者忽都皇后奇氏，高麗人，生皇太子愛猷識理達臘。

translations.literal: Empress Wonjeonghodu, née Ki, was a Korean; she bore Crown Prince Ayushiridara.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wonjeonghodu, née Ki, was Korean and bore Crown Prince Ayushiridara.

sentences.zh: 家微，用后貴，三世皆追封王爵。

translations.literal: Her family was humble; after she became empress they were ennobled, and three generations were all posthumously enfeoffed as kings.
translations.idiomatic: Her family was humble; after she became empress they were ennobled, and three generations were all posthumously enfeoffed as kings.

sentences.zh: 初，徽政院使禿滿叠兒進為宮女，主供茗飲，以事順帝。

translations.literal: At first Tumen Die'er, commissioner of the Xuanhui Court, presented her as a palace woman in charge of serving tea; she attended Shundi.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tumen Die'er, commissioner of the Xuanhui Court, presented her as a palace woman in charge of serving tea; she attended Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 后性穎黠，日見寵幸。

translations.literal: The empress was clever and sharp; day by day she gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was clever and sharp; day by day she gained favor.

sentences.zh: 後答納失裏皇后方驕妒，數箠辱之。

translations.literal: Later, when Empress Danashili was arrogant and jealous, she repeatedly beat and humiliated her.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Empress Danashili was arrogant and jealous, she repeatedly beat and humiliated her.

sentences.zh: 答納失裏既遇害，帝欲立之，丞相伯顏爭不可。

translations.literal: After Danashili was murdered, the emperor wished to establish her; Chancellor Bayan argued that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: After Danashili was murdered, the emperor wished to establish her as empress; Chancellor Bayan argued that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 伯顏罷相，沙剌班遂請立為第二皇后，居興聖宮，改徽政院為資正院。

translations.literal: When Bayan was dismissed from the chancellorship, Sharaban then requested that she be established as second empress; she dwelt in Xingsheng Palace, and the Xuanhui Court was renamed the Zizheng Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan was dismissed from the chancellorship, Sharaban then requested that she be established as second empress; she dwelt in Xingsheng Palace, and the Xuanhui Court was renamed the Zizheng Court.

sentences.zh: 后無事，則取《女孝經》、史書，訪問歷代皇后之有賢行者為法。

translations.literal: When the empress had no affairs, she would take the 《Classic of Filial Piety for Women》 and historical books and inquire after empresses of past ages who had practiced worthiness, taking them as models.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress had no affairs, she would take the 《Classic of Filial Piety for Women》 and historical books and inquire after empresses of past ages who had practiced worthiness, taking them as models.

sentences.zh: 四方貢獻，或有珍味，輒先遣使薦太廟，然后敢食。

translations.literal: When tribute came from the four quarters and there were rare delicacies, she would first send envoys to offer them at the Grand Temple and only then dare to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute came from the four quarters with rare delicacies, she would first send envoys to offer them at the Grand Temple and only then dare to eat.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，京城大饑，后命官為粥食之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhiping there was great famine in the capital; the empress ordered officials to provide gruel for the people to eat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping 18 there was great famine in the capital; the empress ordered officials to provide gruel for the people to eat.

sentences.zh: 又出金銀粟帛，命資正院使樸不花於京都十一門置冢，葬死者遺骼十餘萬，復命僧建水陸大會度之。

translations.literal: She also contributed gold, silver, grain, and silk and ordered Po Buhua, commissioner of the Zizheng Court, to set up burial mounds at the eleven gates of the capital, interring the exposed bones of more than a hundred thousand dead; she further ordered monks to perform a great water-and-land assembly to deliver their souls.
translations.idiomatic: She also contributed gold, silver, grain, and silk and ordered Po Buhua, commissioner of the Zizheng Court, to set up burial mounds at the eleven gates of the capital, interring the exposed bones of more than a hundred thousand dead; she further ordered monks to perform a great water-and-land assembly to deliver their souls.

sentences.zh: 時帝頗怠於政治，后與皇太子愛猷識理達臘遽謀內禪，遣樸不花諭意丞相太平，太平不答。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was rather slack in government; the empress and Crown Prince Ayushiridara hastily plotted an inner abdication and sent Po Buhua to convey their intent to Chancellor Toqto'a; Toqto'a did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was rather slack in government; the empress and Crown Prince Ayushiridara hastily plotted an inner abdication and sent Po Buhua to convey their intent to Chancellor Toqto'a, who did not reply.

sentences.zh: 復召太平至宮，舉酒賜之，自申前請，太平依違而已，由是后與太子銜之。

translations.literal: They again summoned Toqto'a to the palace, raised wine and bestowed it on him, and personally renewed the former request; Toqto'a only hesitated and equivocated, and therefore the empress and the crown prince bore resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: They again summoned Toqto'a to the palace, raised wine and bestowed it on him, and personally renewed the former request; Toqto'a only hesitated and equivocated, and therefore the empress and the crown prince bore resentment against him.

sentences.zh: 而帝亦知后意，怒而疏之，兩月不見。

translations.literal: The emperor also knew the empress's intent; he was angry and kept her at a distance, not seeing her for two months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also knew the empress's intent; he was angry and kept her at a distance, not seeing her for two months.

sentences.zh: 樸不花因后而寵幸，既被劾黜，后諷御史大夫佛家奴為之辯明。

translations.literal: Po Buhua, through the empress, enjoyed favor; after he was impeached and dismissed, the empress hinted to Censor-in-Chief Foxianu to plead his case.
translations.idiomatic: Po Buhua, through the empress, enjoyed favor; after he was impeached and dismissed, the empress hinted to Censor-in-Chief Foxianu to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 佛家奴乃謀再劾樸不花，后知之，反嗾御史劾佛家奴，謫居潮河。

translations.literal: Foxianu then plotted to impeach Po Buhua again; when the empress learned of it, she in turn incited censors to impeach Foxianu, who was demoted and sent to reside at Chaohe.
translations.idiomatic: Foxianu then plotted to impeach Po Buhua again; when the empress learned of it, she in turn incited censors to impeach Foxianu, who was demoted and sent to reside at Chaohe.

sentences.zh: 初，奇氏之族在高麗者，怙勢驕橫，高麗王怒，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ki's clan in Korea had relied on their power and acted arrogantly; the king of Korea was enraged and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ki's clan in Korea had relied on their power and acted arrogantly; the king of Korea was enraged and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，后謂皇太子曰：「汝何不為我復讎耶？」

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the empress said to the crown prince: "Why do you not avenge me?"
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the empress said to the crown prince, "Why do you not avenge me?"

sentences.zh: 遂立高麗王族人留京師者為王，以奇族之子三寶奴為元子。

translations.literal: They then established as king a member of the Korean royal clan who remained in the capital and made Sanbaonu, son of the Ki clan, heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: They then established as king a member of the Korean royal clan who remained in the capital and made Sanbaonu, son of the Ki clan, heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 遣同知樞密院事崔帖木兒為丞相，用兵一萬，並招倭兵，共往納之。

translations.literal: They sent Cui Tiemuer, associate administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, as chancellor, with ten thousand troops and also recruiting Japanese soldiers, to go together and install him.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Cui Tiemuer, associate administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, as chancellor, with ten thousand troops and also recruiting Japanese soldiers, to go together and install him.

sentences.zh: 過鴨綠水，伏兵四起，乃大敗，余十七騎而還，后大慚。

translations.literal: When they crossed the Yalu River, ambush troops rose on all sides; they suffered a great defeat and returned with only seventeen horsemen remaining; the empress was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: When they crossed the Yalu River, ambush troops rose on all sides; they suffered a great defeat and returned with only seventeen horsemen remaining, and the empress was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 二十四年七月，孛羅帖木兒稱兵犯闕，皇太子出奔冀寧，下令討孛羅帖木兒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year Bolu Temür raised troops and attacked the palace; the crown prince fled to Jining and issued orders to campaign against Bolu Temür.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year Bolu Temür raised troops and attacked the palace; the crown prince fled to Jining and issued orders to campaign against Bolu Temür.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒怒，嗾監察御史武起宗言后外撓國政，奏帝宜遷后出於外，帝不答。

translations.literal: Bolu Temür was enraged and incited Supervising Censor Wu Qizong to say that the empress interfered in state affairs from outside; he memorialized that the emperor should transfer the empress outside, but the emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Bolu Temür was enraged and incited Supervising Censor Wu Qizong to say that the empress interfered in state affairs from outside; he memorialized that the emperor should transfer the empress outside, but the emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 二十五年三月，遂矯制幽於諸色總管府，令其黨姚伯顏不花守之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-fifth year he forged an order and had her confined at the Office of the Commissioner for All Colors, ordering his partisan Yao Bayanbuqa to guard her.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-fifth year he forged an order and had her confined at the Office of the Commissioner for All Colors, ordering his partisan Yao Bayanbuqa to guard her.

sentences.zh: 四月庚寅，孛羅帖木兒逼后還宮，取印章，偽為后書召太子。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the fourth month Bolu Temür forced the empress back to the palace, took the seals, and forged a letter in the empress's hand summoning the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the fourth month Bolu Temür forced the empress back to the palace, took the seals, and forged a letter in the empress's hand summoning the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 后仍回幽所，后又數納美女於孛羅帖木兒，至百日，始還宮。

translations.literal: The empress still returned to the place of confinement; later she repeatedly presented beautiful women to Bolu Temür, and only after a hundred days did she return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress still returned to the place of confinement; later she repeatedly presented beautiful women to Bolu Temür, and only after a hundred days did she return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 及孛羅帖木兒死，召皇太子還京師，后傳旨令廓擴帖木兒以兵擁皇太子入城，欲脅帝禪位。

translations.literal: When Bolu Temür died, the crown prince was summoned back to the capital; the empress transmitted an order for Köke Temür to escort the crown prince into the city with troops, intending to coerce the emperor to abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: When Bolu Temür died, the crown prince was summoned back to the capital; the empress transmitted an order for Köke Temür to escort the crown prince into the city with troops, intending to coerce the emperor to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 廓擴帖木兒知其意，至京城三十里外，即遣軍還營，皇太子復銜之。

translations.literal: Köke Temür knew her intent; when he reached thirty li outside the capital he at once sent the army back to camp, and the crown prince again bore resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür knew her intent; when he reached thirty li outside the capital he at once sent the army back to camp, and the crown prince again bore resentment against him.

sentences.zh: 事見《擴廓帖木兒傳》。

translations.literal: The matter is seen in the 《Biography of Köke Temür》.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is treated in the 《Biography of Köke Temür》.

sentences.zh: 會伯顏忽都皇后崩，十二月，中書省臣奏言，后宜正位中宮，帝不答。

translations.literal: When Empress Bayan Qudu died, in the twelfth month ministers of the Secretariat memorialized that the empress should take the correct position in the principal palace; the emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Bayan Qudu died, in the twelfth month ministers of the Secretariat memorialized that the empress should take the principal palace; the emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 又奏改資正院為崇政院，而中政院亦兼主之，帝乃授之冊寶，其冊文曰：「坤以承乾元，人道莫先於夫婦；

translations.literal: They again memorialized to change the Zizheng Court to the Chongzheng Court and have the Central Palace Administration also jointly administer it; the emperor then invested her with registers and seals. The patent read: "Kun receives the origin of Qian; in human relations nothing comes before husband and wife;
translations.idiomatic: They again memorialized to change the Zizheng Court to the Chongzheng Court and have the Central Palace Administration also jointly administer it; the emperor then invested her with registers and seals. The enfeoffment text read: "Earth receives the origin of heaven; in human relations nothing comes before husband and wife;

sentences.zh: 后以母天下，王化實始於家邦。

translations.literal: the empress mothers the realm, and kingly transformation truly begins in family and state.
translations.idiomatic: the empress mothers the realm, and kingly transformation truly begins in family and state.

sentences.zh: 典禮之常，古今攸重。

translations.literal: The constants of ritual are weighty in antiquity and today alike.
translations.idiomatic: The constants of ritual are weighty in antiquity and today alike.

sentences.zh: 咨爾肅良合氏，篤生名族，來事朕躬。

translations.literal: We address you of the Sukorghatas clan, born of a renowned house, come to serve Our person.
translations.idiomatic: We address you of the Sukorghatas clan, born of a renowned house, come to serve our person.

sentences.zh: 儆戒相成，每勤於夙夜；

translations.literal: Admonition and caution complete one another; you are diligent from morning to night;
translations.idiomatic: Admonition and caution complete one another; you are diligent from morning to night;

sentences.zh: 恭儉率下，多歷於歲年。

translations.literal: respectful and frugal, you lead those below, having passed through many years.
translations.idiomatic: respectful and frugal, you lead those below, having passed through many years.

sentences.zh: 既發祥元子於儲闈，復流慶孫枝於甲觀。

translations.literal: You have already sent forth auspicious signs with the eldest son in the heir's quarters and further spread blessing to the grandson-branch in the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: You have already sent forth auspicious signs with the eldest son in the heir's quarters and further spread blessing to the grandson-branch in the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 眷若中宮之位，允宜淑配之賢。

translations.literal: Cherishing the position of the principal palace, you are truly fit to be the worthy consort.
translations.idiomatic: Cherishing the position of the principal palace, you are truly fit to be the worthy consort.

sentences.zh: 宗戚大臣，況僉言而敷請；

translations.literal: Kinsmen and great ministers, moreover, unanimously spoke and broadly petitioned;
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen and great ministers, moreover, unanimously spoke and broadly petitioned;

sentences.zh: 掖庭諸禦，咸傾望以推尊。

translations.literal: all the attendants of the inner quarters alike inclined their hopes to exalt you.
translations.idiomatic: all the attendants of the inner quarters alike inclined their hopes to exalt you.

sentences.zh: 乃屢遜辭，尤可嘉尚。

translations.literal: You repeatedly declined with modest words — especially worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: You repeatedly declined with modest words — especially worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 今遣攝太尉某持節授以玉冊玉寶，命爾為皇后。

translations.literal: Now We send the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies with credentials to confer jade registers and jade seals and command you to be empress.
translations.idiomatic: Now we send the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies with credentials to confer jade registers and jade seals and command you to be empress.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 慎修壸政，益勉爾輔佐之心；

translations.literal: Be careful in cultivating inner governance and further strive in your heart to assist;
translations.idiomatic: Be careful in cultivating inner governance and further strive in your heart to assist;

sentences.zh: 昭嗣徽音，同保我延洪之福。

translations.literal: make manifest the continuation of fine repute and together preserve Our far-reaching blessing.
translations.idiomatic: make manifest the continuation of fine repute and together preserve our far-reaching blessing.

sentences.zh: 其欽寵命，以衍壽祺。」

translations.literal: Reverently receive the favored mandate to extend long life and good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Reverently receive the favored mandate to extend long life and good fortune."

sentences.zh: 二十八年，從帝北奔。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year she followed the emperor in flight to the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year she followed the emperor in flight to the north.
